dict.string: Vox uses Bluetooth to notice when you come home to your paired Mac, so the Mac can greet you. It only looks for your own Mac.
Vox uses the camera to scan your Mac's pairing code and for a private local preview. It sends a still frame only when you ask Vox to look.

Vox uses your location in the background for two things you turn on: place reminders that phone you, which need to notice when you arrive or leave even while Vox is closed (only the fact that a reminder went off is sent to Vox), and, if you turn on location sharing, showing where this iPhone last was on your map in Vox.

Vox uses your location to save places like Home and find nearby stores for place reminders, which stay on this iPhone. If you turn on location sharing, Vox also shows where this iPhone last was on your map in Vox.
Vox uses the microphone so you can have a live voice conversation.
